Goal: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

Hypothesis to revise: TITLE: Label-proportion MIL on mosaics: abnormal mass must scale with the number of abnormal quadrants
SUMMARY: Build mosaics with a known number of abnormal quadrants and add a learning-from-label-proportions loss: the predicted abnormal mass of a mosaic must equal the sum of the per-image abnormal masses of its quadrants' source images when each is seen alone, which ties the segmentation maps' area to image content across contexts.
HYPOTHESIS: Adding the label-proportion consistency loss to mosaic MIL reduces the error of predicted lesion area (relative to true mask area on held-out masked modalities) by at least 25% and raises AUPRO by at least 2 points, while image AUROC changes by less than 1 point.
RATIONALE: Mosaic MIL gives free quadrant labels, and witness-rate MIL shows that the amount of lesion per image matters. A different mechanism combines these hints: learning from label proportions. If a mosaic contains n abnormal images, its abnormal mass should be the sum of the masses of those images seen individually, and the normal quadrants should contribute none. This consistency between single images and their mosaics constrains how much area the adapters mark as abnormal — a quantity no image-level loss controls and that AUPRO directly rewards — without any mask.
METHOD: 1) dataset/mosaic.py as in mosaic MIL (2x2, 120 px quadrants, 1-3 abnormal). 2) For each mosaic, also forward its four source images individually (resized to 120 px, no gradient through the single-image pass). 3) loss.py: lp_loss = | sum_j p_j(mosaic) - sum_q sum_j p_j(image_q) | / number of patches, plus BCE towards 0 on normal quadrants and consensus top-k MIL inside abnormal quadrants. 4) Hyper-parameters: lp weight {0.1, 0.5}; mosaic probability 0.5. Inference unchanged.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: mosaic MIL; consensus MIL. Metric added: relative lesion-area error on held-out masked datasets. Falsified if the area error is not reduced.
